contentBlocks.text: Remember Langar, the free kitchen we talked about? One reason Langar is so special is that everyone sits together as equals — no matter who they are. Today we'll talk about equality, one of the most important ideas in Sikhi.

Equality means that every single person deserves the same respect and kindness, no matter their background, how much money their family has, or anything else about them. At Langar, a business owner might sit right next to someone who has very little — everyone eats the same food, sitting at the same level. Can you think of a way you could treat everyone around you with that same equal respect, at school or at home?
Treating everyone as equal is a value you can practice every day, not just at the Gurdwara. This week, notice one chance to treat someone with that same equal respect and kindness.

objectives: Explain in simple words what equality means (everyone deserves the same respect and kindness)
Connect equality back to Langar as a real, lived example, and identify a new way to practice it
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review what the child remembers about Langar from the first lesson this week.
2. Introduce equality: everyone sitting together at Langar as one example of treating everyone the same, no matter their background.
3. Discuss what equality could look like outside the Gurdwara — at school, with friends, at home.
4. Move to the worksheet: trace the word and talk through its meaning again.
5. Close by picking one specific way to practice equality this week.
differentiationTips: Struggling: stick with the Langar example as the main anchor, rather than introducing many abstract scenarios
Ready for more: discuss a time they saw someone treated unfairly and what equality would have looked like instead
For a child who enjoys connecting ideas, ask how equality relates to Seva and Sangat, both learned earlier this week
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a tracing and discussion activity — there is no right/wrong answer beyond correct word tracing. Check that the child can explain equality in their own words and connect it back to Langar.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Equality is one of the foundational, universally-taught values of Sikhi — grounding it in the already-familiar example of Langar (from this week's first lesson) builds a concrete, connected understanding rather than an abstract, isolated concept.

generationData.instructions: Trace the word, say it out loud, then write it once more on your own.
